issues.issue: Whether a toxic psychosis caused by self-induced intoxication qualifies as a 'mental disorder' under s. 16 Cr.
issues.applicant_position: Argues toxic psychosis from intoxication can be a mental disorder; Cooper’s exclusion applies only to normal intoxication effects.
issues.respondent_position: Contends toxic psychosis from intoxication is not a 'disease of the mind' under s. 16 Cr., especially when caused solely by self-induced intoxication.
issues.result_text: The court finds toxic psychosis from intoxication is not a 'mental disorder' under s. 16 Cr.

issues.issue: Does s. 33.1 Cr. C. limit the scope of the mental disorder defence in s. 16 Cr. C. when the accused is intoxicated?
issues.applicant_position: Claims s. 33.1 does not limit s. 16; intoxication and mental disorder are distinct; s. 33.1 limits only certain offences.
issues.respondent_position: Argues s. 33.1 limits the mental disorder defence; the Court of Appeal erred in not applying s. 33.1.
issues.result_text: S. 33.1 does not limit the scope of s. 16; intoxication and mental disorder are mutually exclusive.

issues.issue: Whether the toxic psychosis from intoxication can be considered a 'mental disorder' under s. 16 Cr. C. in the context of the holistic, case-by-case approach?
issues.applicant_position: Argues that toxic psychosis should be considered a mental disorder; the case law supports a case-by-case analysis.
issues.respondent_position: Contends that toxic psychosis from intoxication is generally not a disease of the mind; each case must be individually assessed.
issues.result_text: A case-by-case, holistic approach is required; toxic psychosis from intoxication generally not a 'disease of the mind'.
